event_code_setup_description: If your event is listed on events.vex.com, enter the event code below which can be found in the event page on events.vex.com.
event_code_setup_description_2: Judges' Room will automatically import many settings for your event. In addition, please enable the feature to publish live results to VEX Events in the Web Publish Setup page of Tournament Manager. This way, Judges' Room can automatically calculate the team eligibility for Excellence Awards and Think Award based on the latest rankings and skills scores.
event_code_setup_description_3: If your event will have two or more divisions:
event_code_setup_description_4: Please use Tournament Manager to set the division for each team and publish the division results to VEX Events first. Judges' Room needs to know which teams belong to which division before it starts.
event_code_setup_description_5: Each Judges' Room can only be used for one division. Please use a second computer, another browser or incognito mode to create another Judges' Room for the second division.
event_code_setup_description_6: Judges' Room can only calculate Excellence Award(s) for its own division (division specific). If your event has event wide Excellence Award(s), please refer to the "Excellence Award Eligibility" reports from the Reports tab in Tournament Manager.
official_event_description: Connect to VEX Events and determine the team eligibility based on the live results.
unofficial_event_description: Continue without connecting to VEX Events.
delete_judge_group_message: Are you sure you want to delete this judge group? If this judge group has been used for judging, all related rubrics and award rankings will be lost forever. This action cannot be undone.
remove_judge_message: Are you sure you want to remove this judge? If this judge submitted any rubrics, they will be lost forever.
walk_in_judging_description: Teams queue up and are assigned to judge groups randomly.
pre_assigned_judging_description: Teams are pre-assigned to specific judge groups. Judges find their assigned teams in their team pits for interviews.
all_active_teams_assigned_to_judge_group: All active teams are assigned to judge groups
drag_and_drop_teams_description: Drag and drop teams from here to judge groups. Right-click to select multiple teams.
all_teams_assigned_to_judge_groups: All teams are assigned to judge groups
please_create_at_least_one_judge_group: Please create at least one judge group to continue.
please_assign_all_active_teams: Please assign all active teams to judge groups to continue.
how_do_you_want_to_import_from_roboteven: How do you want to import from VEX Events?
import_teams_description: Import team list only. Existing teams not in the import will be removed along with their judging data. Teams with matching numbers will preserve their existing data.
import_full_setup_description: Import both teams and awards. The award list will be reset and you'll need to reconfigure custom awards. Awards with matching names will preserve their rankings.
organize_teams_description: Drag and drop teams between groups to organize them. Right click to select multiple teams. Team groups are useful when determining the final ranking of award winners.
no_teams_available: No teams available. Please import teams in the previous step.
choose_your_identity_to_start_participat: Choose your identity to start participating in the Judges' Room. You can change your role at any time later if needed.
evaluate_teams_and_participate_in_scorin: Evaluate teams and participate in scoring
manage_the_judges_room_and_oversee_judge: Manage the Judges' Room and oversee judges
no_judges_have_been_set_up_yet: No judges have been set up yet.
you_can_add_your_name_instead: You can add your name instead.
as_a_judge_advisor_you_can: As a Judge Advisor, you can manage the Judges' Room, oversee all judges, and access all judging data.
award_nominations_description: After judge groups complete their team interviews, each group selects their top one or two candidates from their interviewed teams for each award. Judge groups should share their nominations to create a shortlist for each award. When there are many nominations, the Judge Advisor may ask groups to withdraw weaker candidates based on brief arguments comparing the merits of each nomination against award criteria.
excellence_award_winners_are_selected_fr: Excellence Award winners are selected from Design Award finalists. Nominate teams for each award first, then go to
award_candidate_ranking_description: Click on any ranking cell, then use the minus (-) and plus (+) buttons to adjust stars, this indicates teams that are strong candidates for awards. In award deliberations, all judge groups will cross-reference their lists to create a final award nomination list. This table is shared and synchronized within your judge group - all judges see updates in real-time without having to refresh the page.
copy_this_report_to_share_the_award_winn: Copy this report to share the award winners.
award_winner_tab_description: The Judge Advisor should enter all award winners below for final confirmation. Before the award ceremony, the Judge Advisor should enter the result to the Tournament Manager.
award_winner_tab_performance_awards_desc: Performance Awards are based on robot performance on the competition field in match play and Skills Challenges. These awards do not impact a team's eligibility to earn a Judged Award.
no_performance_awards_configured_for_thi: No performance awards configured for this event.
award_winner_tab_volunteer_nominated_awa: Nominated Awards are determined by nominations from event staff and judges based on observations during the event. These awards are outside the Judged Award deliberation flow. Teams may receive a Nominated Award in addition to a Judged Award.
no_volunteer_nominated_awards_configured: No Nominated Awards configured for this event.
award_winner_tab_summary_of_award_winner: This summary shows all award winners organized by team group.
please_enter_a_valid_url_for_the_noteboo: Please enter a valid URL for the notebook link
failed_to_save_team_data_please_try_agai: Failed to save team data. Please try again.
enter_the_url_to_the_team_s_engineering_: Enter the URL to the team's engineering notebook
failed_to_get_event_from_robotevents: Failed to get event from VEX Events
excellence_award_candidates_description1: The Excellence Award Candidates tab shows the teams that are eligible for the Excellence Award.
excellence_award_candidates_description2: For events with a single Excellence Award, percentages are based on the number of teams at the event. For blended grade level events with two grade specific Excellence Awards, percentages are based on the teams in each grade level for each award. Please double-check the type of event. The Judge Advisor can configure the number of Excellence Award winners by clicking the top right menu and selecting "Change Event Setup".
excellence_award_candidates_description3: For most of the events, all teams are in the same default division: Division 1. If your event has multiple divisions, Judges' Room can only calculate Excellence Award(s) for its own division (division specific). If your event has event wide Excellence Award(s), please refer to the "Excellence Award Eligibility" reports from the Reports tab in Tournament Manager.
excellence_award_candidates_description4: Please refer to the Award Descriptions article in the GRSF judging guidelines for more details regarding the key criteria of the Excellence Award. It is also recommended to use the "Excellence Award Eligibility" reports to verify the results.
excellence_award_candidates_description5: Eligible teams are highlighted in green.
excellence_award_candidates_provisional: Award deliberations have not started yet, so these standings are provisional. Qualification and skills rankings can still change, and with them who is eligible.
excellence_award_candidates_description6: There are {teamsInGroupCount} teams in the {acceptedGrade} grade level in Division {divisionId}. At the conclusion of Qualification Matches, teams must be ranked in the top 40% of teams in this group in Qualification Match rankings. This is calculated by {teamsInGroupCount} * 40% = {rankingEligibilityIntermediate} rounded to {rankingEligibilityThreshold} teams.
excellence_award_candidates_description7: There are {joinedTeamsInEventCount} teams in the {acceptedGrade} grade level at the event. This is the number of teams that actually arrived and participated in Qualification Matches. At the conclusion of the Robot Skills Challenge matches, teams must be ranked in the top 40% of all {acceptedGrade} teams at the event. This is calculated by {joinedTeamsInEventCount} * 40% = {skillsEligibilityIntermediate} rounded to {skillsEligibilityThreshold} teams.
excellence_award_candidates_description8: At the conclusion of the Autonomous Coding Skills Challenge matches, teams must be with a score above 0 and ranked in the top 40% of all {acceptedGrade} teams at the event. This is calculated by {joinedTeamsInEventCount} * 40% = {skillsEligibilityIntermediate} rounded to {skillsEligibilityThreshold} teams.
excellence_award_candidates_description9: There are {teamsInGroupCount} teams in all grade levels in Division {divisionId}. At the conclusion of Qualification Matches, teams must be ranked in the top 40% of teams in this group in Qualification Match rankings. This is calculated by {teamsInGroupCount} * 40% = {rankingEligibilityIntermediate} rounded to {rankingEligibilityThreshold} teams.
excellence_award_candidates_description1: There are {joinedTeamsInEventCount} teams in all grade levels at the event. This is the number of teams that actually arrived and participated in Qualification Matches. At the conclusion of the Robot Skills Challenge matches, teams must be ranked in the top 40% of all teams at the event. This is calculated by {joinedTeamsInEventCount} * 40% = {skillsEligibilityIntermediate} rounded to {skillsEligibilityThreshold} teams.

At the conclusion of the Autonomous Coding Skills Challenge matches, teams must be with a score above 0 and ranked in the top 40% of all teams at the event. This is calculated by {joinedTeamsInEventCount} * 40% = {skillsEligibilityIntermediate} rounded to {skillsEligibilityThreshold} teams.
no_teams_are_eligible_for_this_award: No teams are eligible for this award. It should not be given out at the event.
failed_to_get_excellence_award_eligibili: Failed to get Excellence Award eligibility data from VEX Events
final_ranking_description1: Create the final ranking of award winners from nominated teams. After follow-up interviews are completed, judges who conducted those interviews should deliberate and rank nominees for each award. It's best practice to have first-choice winners plus three or more alternate candidates. Drag and drop teams to reorder nominations.
final_ranking_description2: Excellence Award winners are selected from Design Award finalists who also meet Performance Award criteria, which may result in reshuffling other award winners to maintain the one-judged-award-per-team rule. Drag team(s) from the Design Award column to the Excellence Award column(s) to designate Excellence Award winner(s).
final_ranking_description3: Teams in Excellence Award and Design Award columns display eligibility indicators in the top-right corner: <green>≤40%</green> (green) indicates the team meets the performance criteria (top 40% in qualification rankings, robot skills, and autonomous coding skills), <red>>40%</red> (red) indicates they do not meet the criteria.
final_ranking_description4: Teams in Think Award column display eligibility indicators in the top-right corner: <green>AUTO✓</green> (green) indicates the team participated in the Autonomous Coding Skills Challenge with a score greater than zero, <red>AUTO✗</red> (red) indicates they do not meet this criteria.
final_ranking_description5: Please make sure to enable the feature to publish live results to VEX Events in the Web Publish Setup page of Tournament Manager. Click "Refresh from VEX Events" to update the eligibility status.
final_ranking_description6: This Judges' Room failed to fetch the eligibility data from VEX Events. Please check the Internet connection and try again.
final_ranking_description7: This Judges' Room is not connected to VEX Events. To enable eligibility checking, please configure the VEX Events Event ID and Division ID in Event Setup.
final_ranking_description8: Winning teams for each award are marked with a colored border: <green>green</green> for eligible winners, <red>red</red> for ineligible winners, and <slate>gray</slate> when eligibility data is unavailable.
judges_room_not_connected_to_robotevents: This tool helps judges and judge advisors to identify the candidates for Excellence Awards by fetching the latest rankings and skills scores from VEX Events. However, this Judges' Room is not connected to VEX Events.

match.notFoundCount=0: Successfully updated notebook links for {count} teams

notebook_links_import_error: No teams were found matching the Excel data
notebook_sorting_description1: Judges perform a quick scan of all the Engineering Notebooks and divide them into three categories: Not Submitted, Developing, and Fully Developed. If it is unclear whether a notebook should be categorized as Developing or Fully Developed, either another Judge can help make that determination or the notebook should be given the benefit of the doubt and categorized as Fully Developed.
notebook_sorting_description2: After sorting, evaluate all Developing and Fully Developed notebooks using the Engineering Notebook Rubric.
notebook_sorting_description3: Under GRSF, Fully Developed status is still required for Design, Innovate, and Excellence Award eligibility.
notebook_sorting_description4: Under GRSF, the Innovate Award Submission Form is not tracked during notebook sorting and is not required for Innovate Award eligibility.
notebook_sorting_description5: If notebooks were submitted digitally, a team with a notebook link can be scored without being sorted first. Open its rubric, read the notebook, and record whether it is Developing or Fully Developed when you submit.
notebook_sorting_import_title: Import Digital Engineering Notebook Links report
notebook_sorting_import_description1: If Engineering Notebooks are submitted digitally, please ask the Event Partner to provide digital notebook links report. This report can be downloaded from VEX Events → Event Admin → "Downloads & Links" → "Download Digital Engineering Notebook Links report". Import the Excel file to this Judges' Room to set notebook links for teams in your event.
only_show_assigned_teams_for_your_curren: Only show assigned teams for your current judge group ({name})
only_show_notebooks_with_season_summary: Only show notebooks submitted with a Season Summary
season_summary_badge_title: Submitted with a Season Summary, so this notebook is scored first
failed_to_update_season_summary: Failed to record whether a Season Summary was submitted
notebook_development_status_score: Team {teamNumber} scored {score} out of {maxScore} on the Engineering Notebook Rubric.
notebook_development_status_benchmark: A score of {benchmark} or above is a useful guide to Fully Developed. It means the notebook averaged Proficient across all {criteriaCount} criteria. Where the cut falls at your event depends on what was submitted, so treat {benchmark} as a benchmark rather than a rule.
notebook_development_status_why: This decides whether the team is eligible for the Design, Innovate and Excellence Awards. You can change it later on the Notebook Sorting tab.
failed_to_record_notebook_development_st: Failed to record how developed the notebook is
no_teams_assigned_to_your_judge_group: No teams are assigned to your judge group.
failed_to_update_innovate_award_submissi: Failed to update innovate award submission form
start_award_deliberation_message: This will unlock award deliberation functions for all judges for the last step in the judging process. Rubrics can still be submitted. Please confirm to proceed.
award_deliberation_started: Award deliberation started! All judges can now access award deliberation functions.

excellence_award_candidates_description: Check the eligibility of each team
open_qr_code_dialog: Open a dialog with a QR code for the link
manual_attendance_changes_disabled_for_r: Manual attendance changes are disabled for VEX Events integrated events. Use the sync button to update from VEX Events.
no_team_rankings_found: No team rankings found. Please check-in teams in Tournament Manager and generate the match schedule first.
found_teams_with_rankings_some_attendanc: Found {count} teams with rankings. Some attendance differences detected.
found_teams_with_rankings_attendance_syn: Found {count} teams with rankings. Attendance is synchronized.
failed_to_fetch_attendance_from_roboteve: Failed to fetch attendance from VEX Events: {error}
team_attendance_synchronized_with_robote: Team attendance synchronized with VEX Events!
team_attendance_description_robotevents_: Manage the team attendance is important for the later stages of the judging process. This Judges' Room is connected to VEX Events. Click the "Refresh from VEX Events" button to update the team attendance. Please make sure to enable the feature to publish live results to VEX Events in the Web Publish Setup page of Tournament Manager.
team_attendance_description_manual: Manage the team attendance is important for the later stages of the judging process. Click the top right button of a team to mark it as present or absent.
some_teams_have_different_attendance_sta: Some teams have different attendance status between the judging system and VEX Events. Teams with flashing borders show the differences.
destroy_judging_data_description: Prior to the award ceremony, the Judge Advisor should secure the Judges' Room and destroy all judging materials. These items are not to be given to the Event Partner for destruction.
destroy_judging_data_description_warning: This action will permanently destroy all judging data including team evaluations, rankings, notes, and interview photos. Make sure all connected devices have completed judging and all data has been properly collected before proceeding.
destroy_judging_data_confirmation: Type 'destroy' below to confirm the permanent destruction of all judging data.
choose_your_new_identity_for_the_judges_: Choose your new identity for the Judges' Room.
send_the_link_to_other_judges_to_invite_: Send the link to other judges to invite them to join
or_have_them_scan_the_qr_code_with_their: Or have them scan the QR code with their phone camera
all_participants_will_see_real_time_upda: All participants will see real-time updates
you_are_disconnected_from_the_server: You are disconnected from the server. This may be due to a network issue.
are_you_sure_you_want_to_leave_the_judge: Are you sure you want to leave the Judges' Room? You will lose connection to other judges.
this_action_is_available_for_judge_advis: This action is available for Judge Advisors only.
are_you_sure_you_want_to_modify_the_even: Are you sure you want to modify the event setup? This could disrupt ongoing judging activities.
you_have_unsaved_changes: You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to close this tab?
failed_to_reconnect_to_judges_room: Failed to reconnect to Judges' Room: {error}
you_have_been_kicked_from_the_judges_roo: You have been kicked from the Judges' Room
the_judges_room_has_been_destroyed: The Judges' Room has been destroyed
please_complete_all_scoring_sections: Please complete all scoring sections before submitting the rubric.
failed_to_save_team_interview_rubric: Failed to save team interview rubric
absent_team_description: This team has been marked as absent. They are not eligible for any Judged Awards.
please_switch_to_a_judge: (Please switch to a judge in order to submit the rubric)
team_interview_rubric_directions: Directions: Score what you hear during the conversation. For each criterion, choose Heard, with Specifics (2 points), Heard (1 point), or Not Yet Heard (0 points). The listen-fors are examples of the kinds of evidence that count — you do not need to hear all of them, and hearing any one of them counts. Please refer to the Team Interview Rubrics article in the GRSF judging guidelines for more information.
judging_materials_strictly_confidential_: All judging materials are strictly confidential. They are not shared beyond the Judges and Judge Advisor and shall be destroyed at the end of the event.
rubric_award_candidate_ranking_descripti: Rate this team for specific awards based on your team interview by clicking on the boxes below. Indicate how strong a candidate this team is for each award using the star system (0-5 stars). This table is shared and synchronized within your judge group - all judges see updates in real-time without having to refresh the page.
notebook_development_status_warning: This team did not submit an Engineering Notebook, or its notebook status is undetermined. This notebook will be marked as Developing if the rubric is submitted.
notebook_rubric_directions: Directions: Determine the point value that best characterizes the content of the Engineering Notebook for that criterion. Write that value in the column to the right. This rubric is to be used for all Engineering Notebooks regardless of format (physical or digital). Please refer to the Engineering Notebook Rubrics article in the GRSF judging guidelines for information on how to use this rubric.
notebook_rubric_notes: Notes: Any Student-Centered or Code of Conduct concerns, such as plagiarism, should be brought to the attention of the Judge Advisor and/or Event Partner.
notebook_rubric_award_candidate_ranking_: Rate this team for specific awards based on your notebook review by clicking on the boxes below. Indicate how strong a candidate this team is for each award using the star system (0-5 stars). This table is shared and synchronized within your judge group - all judges see updates in real-time without having to refresh the page.
rubric_ti_sample_questions_title: Sample Questions — Choose 2-3 questions to guide students to meet the criteria.
rubric_ti_q_explain_1: Pick a part of your robot or code, walk me through how it works and why you built it that way.
rubric_ti_q_explain_2: Tell me about a problem that took more than one try. What did you try?
rubric_ti_q_explain_3: What’s something you built or coded that you ended up throwing away?
rubric_ti_q_explain_4: How do you know that works?
rubric_ti_q_explain_5: What can you do now that you couldn’t at the start of the season?
rubric_ti_q_others_2: What’s something you taught a teammate this season?
rubric_ti_q_others_3: Tell me about a time your team disagreed about what to do. How did you decide?
rubric_ti_q_others_4: Where did the idea for that come from? What did you change about it?
rubric_ti_q_others_5: Which other team(s) have you learned something from?
rubric_ti_criteria_header: Criteria and What to Listen For
rubric_ti_listen_fors_note: Listen-fors are examples of the kinds of evidence that count for a row. You do not need to hear all of them.
rubric_ti_desc_not_yet: Team could not address it, even after a question
rubric_ti_explain_own_work_listen_1: how a part of the robot, code, or strategy works
rubric_ti_explain_own_work_listen_2: questions land with the student who can answer — no one has to explain everything
rubric_ti_explain_own_work_listen_3: why the team built it that way
rubric_ti_explain_trace: Students trace how they got there.
rubric_ti_explain_trace_listen_2: something that did not work, and what they did next
rubric_ti_explain_trace_listen_3: a moment that changed their thinking — a test, a failure, a conversation
rubric_ti_explain_evidence: Students show how they know it works.
rubric_ti_explain_evidence_listen_3: a test that changed the design
rubric_ti_others_learned: Students learned from and with each other.
rubric_ti_others_learned_listen_1: one student taught another a useable skill
rubric_ti_others_learned_listen_2: students add to/extend each other’s answers
rubric_ti_others_decisions_listen_1: how the team reached a decision
rubric_ti_others_decisions_listen_2: a disagreement and how it was settled
rubric_ti_others_decisions_listen_3: decisions made by students, not for them
rubric_ti_others_outside_ideas: Outside ideas were made their own.
rubric_ti_others_outside_ideas_listen_1: where an idea came from — another team, a video, a mentor (credit)
rubric_ti_others_outside_ideas_listen_2: what they changed to fit their robot (adapt)
rubric_ti_others_outside_ideas_listen_3: how they tested it on their robot (test)
home_hero_subtitle: Judging and Referee Tools for VEX Robotics Competitions
home_hero_description: Run judging without paper. Digital rubrics, nominations and award deliberations, with confidential materials kept secure and destroyed when the event ends.
home_cta_description: Set up an event, or open a Judges' Room or referee notes you have been invited to.
rubric_print_license: Licensed under GPLv3. robotools.app is a free and open-source project.
delete_photo_message: Are you sure you want to delete this photo? This cannot be undone.
photo_limit_reached: Maximum of {count} photos per team reached
devices_access_link_instructions: Scan this QR code or open the link on your phone or tablet to join the judges room as your identity. Treat it like a password, do not share it with anyone else.
users_dialog_description: Copy or rotate each person’s access link. Connected devices appear under the user they signed in as.
save_your_access_link: Save your Judge Advisor access link
save_your_access_link_warning: If you lose this link, you will not be able to rejoin as Judge Advisor. Store it somewhere safe and do not share it with judges.
rotate_access_link_confirm: Rotate this access link? Devices using the old link will be kicked and must use the new link.
rotate_judge_advisor_access_link_confirm: Rotate the Judge Advisor access link? All other Judge Advisors will be kicked except you. They will need to join again with the new link.
your_judge_role_has_been_removed_please_: Your judge role has been removed from the event setup. Please select a new role.
your_judge_access_was_revoked_ask_ja_for: Your judge access was revoked. Ask the Judge Advisor for a new access link.
you_can_only_edit_your_own_rubrics: You can only edit rubrics you authored.
delete_rubric_message: This permanently deletes {judgeName}’s {rubricKind} for team {teamNumber}, including its scores and notes. It cannot be undone, and the judge will have to enter it again. Their award candidate stars are kept — those belong to the judge group rather than to this rubric.
delete_rubric_last_warning: This is the only submission your group holds for team {teamNumber}, so the team will go back to needing review.
switching_roles_disabled_with_access_con: Switching roles is disabled when access control is enabled. Use your personal access link on another device if needed.
judges_overview_description: Review who is judging, which group they are in, and which teams each group covers.
remove_judge_confirmation: Remove {name} from this Judges' Room? Their submitted rubrics are kept, but their access link stops working and any device signed in as them is disconnected.
remove_judge_group_confirmation: Remove the group {name}? Its assigned teams become unassigned. Move or remove its judges first.
randomly_assign_unassigned_teams_confirm: Spread these {count} unassigned teams at random across the {groups} judge groups, evening out how many teams each group covers? Teams already assigned to a group are not moved, and you can still drag any team afterwards.
no_teams_assigned: No teams assigned to this group yet.
no_judges_in_group: No judges in this group yet.
at_least_one_judge_group: A Judges' Room needs at least one judge group.
remove_judge_advisor_confirmation: Remove {name} as a Judge Advisor? Their access link stops working immediately and any device signed in as them is disconnected.
switch_event_description: Rooms on this device. Each division is its own Judges' Room with its own teams, judges and data.
new_event_copy_setup_description: Copying brings across this event's awards, judge groups and details, ready for another division's teams.
event_group_description: An event group ties the divisions of one competition together, so one Judge Advisor link opens all of them. Judging data stays in its own division.
event_group_not_joined: This division is not part of an event group.
event_group_read_only: You are here through this division's own access link. Managing the group needs a group link.
leave_event_group_confirmation: Remove this division from its event group? Group Judge Advisors lose access to this division immediately. Its own Judge Advisors and all judging data are unaffected.
invalid_event_group_link: That is not a valid event group link.
paste_judges_room_or_group_link: Paste a Judges' Room or event group link:
remove_group_advisor_confirmation: Remove {name} from the event group? Their link stops working for every division immediately.
remove_division_confirmation: Remove {name} from the event group? Group Judge Advisors lose access to it immediately. The division and its judging data are not deleted.
forget_event_group_confirmation: Remove {name} from this device? The event group and its divisions are not deleted — its link opens them again. Divisions you hold on their own access links are kept.
home_features_description: Everything a judging team needs during a competition, and nothing that outlives it.
home_feature_rubrics_description: Team interview and engineering notebook rubrics submitted from any device, with no paper to collect, collate or lose.
home_feature_collaboration_description: Every judge works in the same Judges' Room. Submissions, nominations and rankings appear on every device as they happen.
home_feature_confidentiality_description: Access is controlled per person, deliberation data never leaves its event, and destroying the room destroys everything in it.
access_link_dialog_description: Give this to {name} only. Anyone holding it enters the room as them.
access_link_qr_alt: QR code containing the access link for {name}
access_link_qr_alt_own: QR code containing your own access link
access_link_no_clipboard: Copying needs a secure (HTTPS) connection. Select the link above, or scan the QR code.
theme_description: Dark is easier on the eyes in a dimly lit judging room.
judge_email_invalid: That does not look like an email address
email_all_access_links_confirm: Email every judge who has an address their own access link? Each link signs that judge in, so check the addresses first.
email_send_none_addressed: No judge has an email address yet
enter_judge_names_hint: One per line. Add an address to email their link: Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>
email_not_configured: Emailing links is not set up on this server. Addresses can still be recorded here, and links handed out by QR code.
judge_advisor_step_description: Your name appears to the judges. Your email is used once, to send you your own access link as the event is created — which is the copy you will still have tomorrow.
judge_advisor_email_hint: Your link is how you get back in. Emailing it means you are not relying on the one shown on screen at the end of setup.
judge_advisor_email_missing: Strongly recommended. Without an address, the link shown once at the end of setup is your only copy — nothing inside the event can reissue it, and recovering it means asking whoever operates this server.
email_own_link_confirm: Email your Judge Advisor access link to {email}?
judge_advisor_email_prompt: Judge Advisor email (optional — leave blank to hand the link over yourself):
write_failed: {context} — your change may not have been saved. Check your connection and try again. ({reason})
results_report_description: A record of the outcome that survives destroying the event. Save as PDF from your browser's print dialog.
judge_passes_description: A printable pass for each judge with a QR code for their access link, six to an A4 page. Hand them out in person when links can't be emailed. Save as PDF from your browser's print dialog.
judge_passes_none: There are no judges in this event yet.
pass_personal_note: Please note, this pass is for you only. No sharing with anyone.
ref_passes_description: A printable pass for each referee with a QR code for their link, six to an A4 page. Hand them out in person when links can't be emailed. Save as PDF from your browser's print dialog.
ref_passes_none: There are no referees to print passes for yet.
results_report_empty: No judged awards in this event.
results_report_footer: Rubric scores and judge notes are deliberately not included: they are confidential to the judging panel and are removed when the event is destroyed.
destroy_export_prompt: Export the results first? Destroying deletes everything, and this is the only record you can keep.
matches_description: Match schedule and results for the event
matches_not_linked: This event is not linked to RobotEvents, so there is no match schedule to show. Link it in the event setup to use this tab.
matches_none: No matches have been published for this division yet.
matches_none_for_my_teams: None of your teams are in the published schedule yet.
matches_stale: This schedule may be out of date — the last update failed: {reason}
matches_rankings_none: No rankings have been published for this division yet.
skills_description: Combined driver and programming skills standings
skills_none: No skills runs have been recorded for this event yet.
skills_none_for_my_teams: None of your teams have recorded a skills run yet.
skills_stale: These standings may be out of date — the last update failed: {reason}
free_time_description: When each team next has a break between matches long enough for an interview
free_time_no_schedule: There is no match schedule with times yet, so there are no breaks to show.
free_time_none_for_my_teams: None of your teams are in the match schedule.
free_time_assumption: Allows {before} minutes before each match for queuing and {after} minutes after. Time already passed is left out.
free_time_none_left: No break of {minutes} min or more left today
free_time_running_late: Matches are running about {minutes} min behind schedule, so the times below are moved later to match.
free_time_running_early: Matches are running about {minutes} min ahead of schedule, so the times below are moved earlier to match.
free_time_break: Schedule break: {from} – {until} ({length}). Every team is free then, so it is left out of the times below.
rubric_nb_cat_reflection: Engineering Design Process – Reflection and Iteration
rubric_nb_org_reference_exemplary: Pages are numbered, entries are ordered chronologically or by section, and a table of contents leads to specific entries.
rubric_nb_org_reference_proficient: Pages are numbered with a table of contents, but finding an entry takes searching.
rubric_nb_org_reference_developing: Some organization is present, but locating information is difficult.
rubric_nb_org_reference_beginning: No pagination or table of contents. Information cannot be located.
rubric_nb_org_contributors_exemplary: The team number appears on the notebook, and all entries are signed or initialed by the student who wrote them.
rubric_nb_org_contributors_proficient: The team number appears, and most entries are attributed to a student.
rubric_nb_org_contributors_developing: The team number appears, but entries are rarely attributed.
rubric_nb_org_contributors_beginning: The team number is missing, or entries are not attributed at all.
rubric_nb_org_season_exemplary: Dated entries span the season, demonstrating a consistent habit of notebooking.
rubric_nb_org_season_proficient: Dated entries span the season, showing notebooking habits with some gaps.
rubric_nb_org_season_developing: Entries cluster in a few short periods, or large stretches of the season are missing.
rubric_nb_org_season_beginning: Entries are undated, or all appear to have been created at one time.
rubric_nb_org_sources_exemplary: Outside sources (designs, mechanisms, code, and ideas the team built on) are named where they appear.
rubric_nb_org_sources_proficient: Most outside sources are named, though some appear without credit.
rubric_nb_org_sources_developing: A few sources are named, or credits appear only as a list, not where they were used.
rubric_nb_org_sources_beginning: Outside work appears with no credit.
rubric_nb_define_criteria_exemplary: The notebook defines and explains the problem along with the rules and constraints that could impact possible solutions.
rubric_nb_define_criteria_proficient: The notebook defines a problem without explanation, and lists related criteria and constraints.
rubric_nb_define_criteria_developing: A problem is defined without specific criteria or limits.
rubric_nb_define_criteria_beginning: The problem to be solved is not defined and no criteria and constraints appear.
rubric_nb_define_strategy_exemplary: The notebook describes the team's scoring priorities with reasoning and tradeoffs that come with those priorities.
rubric_nb_define_strategy_proficient: The notebook describes the team's scoring priorities with some reasoning. No tradeoffs are documented.
rubric_nb_define_brainstorm_exemplary: Several distinct approaches (coding, engineering, and/or strategy) are recorded with enough detail to see how they differ.
rubric_nb_define_brainstorm_proficient: Three or more approaches are recorded without comparison, or one or two ideas appear with comparison.
rubric_nb_define_brainstorm_developing: One or two ideas appear with no comparison.
rubric_nb_define_brainstorm_beginning: No brainstorming appears, or a single solution appears already chosen.
rubric_nb_develop_prototypes_exemplary: The notebook shows continuous prototyping with three or more attempts at a solution that clearly connect to one another.
rubric_nb_develop_prototypes_proficient: The notebook shows two or more attempts at a solution with a connection between the attempts.
rubric_nb_develop_prototypes_developing: A single build appears, with little sense of what preceded it.
rubric_nb_develop_tests_exemplary: Tests state what was measured, how, and under what conditions, so the test could be repeated.
rubric_nb_develop_tests_proficient: Tests state what was measured and how.
rubric_nb_develop_tests_developing: Testing is mentioned without saying what was measured or how.
rubric_nb_develop_tests_beginning: No testing is documented, or the robot was tried with no test described.
rubric_nb_develop_data_exemplary: Tests produce recorded qualitative and quantitative results in a form that can be used for data-based decision making.
rubric_nb_develop_data_proficient: Tests record only qualitative or quantitative measurements (not both) to be used for decision making.
rubric_nb_develop_data_developing: Results are described in general terms, without measurements.
rubric_nb_develop_decisions_exemplary: The notebook states what the team decided, how the decision was made, who was part of the decision, and what evidence led to the choice.
rubric_nb_develop_decisions_proficient: Decisions are stated with reasoning and evidence. No indication is made of who was involved in the decision.
rubric_nb_develop_decisions_developing: Decisions appear with little or no reasoning or evidence.
rubric_nb_develop_decisions_beginning: Changes appear with no indication of why.
rubric_nb_optimize_mechanisms_exemplary: Sketches, images, or CAD show a built solution. Descriptive labels show how or why parts of the mechanism exist.
rubric_nb_optimize_mechanisms_proficient: Sketches, images, or CAD show the built solution with basic labels.
rubric_nb_optimize_mechanisms_developing: Images appear without explanation of how or why the mechanism works.
rubric_nb_optimize_mechanisms_beginning: The built solution is not documented.
rubric_nb_optimize_code_exemplary: Pseudocode, flowcharts, annotated screenshots, or commented code show the intention behind the code and how the code was developed.
rubric_nb_optimize_code_proficient: Code is documented in any of these forms, with explanation of the intention behind the code.
rubric_nb_optimize_code_developing: Code appears with little or no explanation.
rubric_nb_optimize_changes_exemplary: Changes to the robot or code follow from recorded test results, and the notebook makes the connection explicit.
rubric_nb_optimize_changes_proficient: Changes follow from testing, though the connection is sometimes implied.
rubric_nb_optimize_changes_developing: Changes and testing both appear, but they are not connected.
rubric_nb_optimize_changes_beginning: Changes appear with no testing behind them.
rubric_nb_reflect_throughout_exemplary: The notebook shows a continuous pattern of reflection throughout the season, and reflections shape what happens next.
rubric_nb_reflect_throughout_proficient: Reflections appear at more than one point in the season.
rubric_nb_reflect_throughout_developing: Reflection appears only at the end, or only as a general summary.
rubric_nb_reflect_throughout_beginning: No reflection appears, or entries record activity without evaluating it.
rubric_nb_reflect_iteration_exemplary: The notebook shows a continuous pattern of iteration throughout the season using the Engineering Design Process for building, strategizing, and coding.
rubric_nb_reflect_iteration_proficient: The notebook shows a pattern of iteration throughout the season in one or two categories (building, strategizing, coding).
rubric_nb_reflect_iteration_developing: The notebook shows some iteration in one of the categories (building, strategizing, coding).
rubric_nb_reflect_iteration_beginning: The notebook shows little to no iteration.
ref_tagline: Log incidents at the field and see every ref's notes as they come in.
ref_have_a_link_description: Your Head Referee sends each ref their own link. Open it on this device, or paste it here.
ref_link_not_recognised: That doesn't look like a ref link. It should contain roomId= and auth=.
ref_create_failed: The event could not be created. Try again in a moment.
ref_join_failed: Could not open the ref room. Check your connection and open your link again.
ref_signed_out_invalid_link: That ref link is no longer valid. Ask your Head Referee for a new one.
ref_signed_out_room_not_found: This ref room no longer exists.
ref_signed_out_access_changed: Your access was changed by the Head Referee. Ask them for your new link.
ref_signed_out_room_destroyed: The Head Referee deleted this event's referee notes.
ref_setup_description: You will be the Head Referee. You can add the other refs once the event is set up.
ref_manual_note: Without VEX Events there is no team list or match schedule. Refs type team numbers and match names themselves.
ref_your_email_supporting: We email your link here so you can get back in on another device.
ref_name_invalid: Enter a name without spaces at the start or end.
ref_email_invalid: That email address doesn't look right.
ref_sign_out_message: This device will forget your ref link for this event. You will need the link again to get back in. Your other events stay saved.
ref_your_events_description: The events this device has a ref link for. Tap one to switch to it.
ref_forget_event_message: This device will forget your ref link for {name}. You will need the link again to get back in.
ref_copy_refs: Also add the other refs from {name} ({count})
ref_copy_refs_description: They get new links for this event. Nothing is emailed until you send their links from Manage.
ref_copy_refs_done_message: Refs added to this event: {count}. Send their links from the Manage tab.
ref_copy_refs_partial_message: Refs added to this event: {count}. These could not be added, so add them from Manage: {failed}.
ref_rules_placeholder: Or type a rule code, e.g. SG6, then Enter
ref_private_description: Only refs see this note. It is never shared with judges.
ref_delete_incident_message: The incident for {team} will be removed for every ref. This cannot be undone.
ref_no_incidents_for_team: No incidents logged for this team.
ref_feed_search: Search team, rule, note or ref
ref_teams_search: Search team number, name or school
ref_no_schedule: There is no match schedule yet. Link the Judges' rooms on the Manage tab to get it, or use Log incident and type the match.
ref_schedule_error: The schedule could not be updated: {error}
ref_matches_hint: Tap a team to log against that match. Tap a badge to see the team's history.
ref_all_played: All matches here have been played.
ref_email_supporting: Used to send them their link. Nothing is sent until you press Email link.
ref_link_replaced: {name} has a new link. The old one no longer works.
ref_replace_link_message: Their current link stops working straight away and any device using it is signed out. Send them the new one afterwards.
ref_remove_ref_message: Their link stops working straight away. Incidents they logged are kept, with their name.
ref_export_description: Download all {count} incidents as a spreadsheet.
ref_update_teams_description: Re-import the team list from VEX Events after late registrations. Currently {count} teams.
ref_delete_event_description: Delete every note, ref and link for this event.
ref_delete_event_message: Every incident, referee and link for this event is deleted for everyone. Linked Judges' Rooms stop seeing these notes. This cannot be undone.
ref_qr_description: Scan with the ref's phone camera. This link is personal to them.
ref_email_all_links_confirm: Email every ref who has an address their own link? Each link signs that ref in, so check the addresses first.
ref_email_none_addressed: No ref has an email address yet
ref_email_not_configured: Emailing links is not set up on this server. You can still record addresses, and hand out links by copying them or showing the QR code.
ref_link_description: Linking gives the Head Referee's notes app this division's team list and match schedule. The refs see nothing else from judging.
ref_link_code_instructions: The Head Referee enters this in the referee app, on the Manage tab under Judges' rooms.
ref_link_linked_to: Linked to the referee notes for {name}.
ref_link_unlink_message: The referee app stops getting this division's teams and schedule straight away. You can link it again with a new code.
ref_links_description: Link each division's Judges' Room to get its team list and match schedule here. Ask the Judge Advisor for a code: Menu, then Referee notes.
ref_links_unlink_message: Its team list and schedule stop coming through. Incidents already logged are kept. You can link again with a new code from the Judge Advisor.
ref_link_create_description: Creates referee notes for this event, already linked, and emails the Head Referee their link. You won't see the link yourself.
ref_link_create_needs_email: Email isn't set up on this server, so the Head Referee's link can't be sent. Ask them to set up referee notes and give them a code instead.
ref_link_created_sent: The Head Referee's link was sent to {email}.
ref_link_code_description: Make a one-time code for the Head Referee to enter in the referee app.
ref_notes_overview_description: What the referees logged about this division's teams
ref_notes_tab_description: What the referees logged about this division's teams, as it comes in. Notes the refs kept to themselves are not shown.
ref_notes_not_linked: This division doesn't have referee notes yet. Start them to write down what the refs tell you, or link the Head Referee's notes.
ref_notes_empty: No ref notes for this division's teams yet.
ref_notes_no_match: No ref notes match these filters.
ref_notes_none_for_team: No ref notes for this team.
ref_notes_add_description: Write down what the refs told you. Judge Advisors see it here, and so will the refs if they start using the referee app.
ref_notes_refs_not_using_app: The refs aren't using the referee app for this division, so these notes come from its Judge Advisors. Add what the refs tell you. If the refs start using the app, invite the Head Referee and your notes move across.
ref_notes_judge_card_description: Pass on something about one of your teams
ref_notes_judge_description: Pass on something about one of your teams, such as what they told you happened on the field. Your Judge Advisor will see it. You won't be able to see or change it after sending.
ref_notes_judge_sent: Note about {team} sent to your Judge Advisor.
ref_link_kept_by_advisors: Right now this division's ref notes are written by its Judge Advisors. Invite the Head Referee or give them a code, and the notes you've added move into the refs' app.
ref_rules_search: Search rule code, words or section
ref_rules_manual_note: The manual has the full rule and its notes. It and the official Q&A are the authority.
ref_delete_export_prompt: Export first? All {count} incidents go with the event, and a spreadsheet is the only record you can keep.
